audit: VERTEX Kattis candidate original-statement evidence ledger — pass 9
method: Inspected contest statement copies for title, contest identity, scenario, input/output and constraints. The PRIPREME statement is a contest statement copy; Introspective Caching is the original NCPC 2008 contest PDF. Live Kattis pages remain independently unverified.

records.title: Pripreme
records.identity: COCI statement explicitly identifies Task PRIPREME and its round/date; candidate metadata claims the same COCI 2014/2015 Round 4 provenance
records.observed: Ante and Goran prepare student teams for a programming competition. Each of two lecturers must teach each team sequentially without interruption, and the goal is to minimize total completion time.
records.excerpt: Ante and Goran are preparing N teams of young ambitious students for a student programming competition of students from University of Zagreb.
records.inputOutput: Input: N and the duration each team needs to understand and implement an algorithm. Output: minimum completion time for the two lecturers' schedules.
records.constraints: Each duration is in [1, 3×10^5]; statement does not specify an explicit upper bound for N in the visible excerpt.
records.scenarioNotes: Real scheduling context with two parallel lecturers and team-specific processing times, but one scheduling optimization task. Keep for depth review; not approved as long scenario.

records.title: Introspective Caching
records.identity: Original NCPC 2008 statement explicitly identifies Problem I Introspective Caching; matches submitted contest provenance and Kattis title/slug
records.observed: A distributed system uses a finite cache to avoid repeated network fetches. A fictional precognitive monkey knows all future object accesses and chooses evictions to minimize cache misses.
records.excerpt: In a distributed system, data is never where you need it, and fetching data over a network takes time and consumes bandwidth.
records.inputOutput: Input: cache capacity, number of distinct objects and access sequence. Output: minimum number of times an object must be read into cache.
records.constraints: 0 < c ≤ 10,000; c ≤ n ≤ 100,000; 0 ≤ a ≤ 100,000; each access is an object ID in [0,n−1].
records.scenarioNotes: Clear distributed-systems context, explanatory mechanism, operational objective and large input scale. Strong scenario framing but still one optimal cache-eviction task; retain for human long-scenario review.
